page: Microsoft Azure F32-16amds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine configuration that couples high clock speeds with an extensive memory footprint and direct-attached solid-state storage. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor capable of reaching 4.5 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, complemented by vector extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 for accelerated numerical operations.

Hardware allocations distinguish this instance through a high memory-to-core ratio, delivering 256.0 GB of RAM at 16.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capacity includes an integrated 3,780 GB local NVMe SSD, providing low-latency ephemeral scratch space alongside support for premium remote storage. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on virtual network infrastructure for connectivity.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance driven by the 4.5 GHz clock ceiling. In stress-ng single-core tests, the system placed in the top 10% of recorded results at 3,529.75, matching top-tier rates in single-threaded gzip compression at 38.87 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.39 GB/sec. Small-model LLM inference generation also achieved top-tier throughput at 425.32 tokens per second. In contrast, multi-threaded CPU throughput, large-block memory bandwidth, PassMark aggregate scores, and Redis operations fell within median tiers, reflecting the 16-thread cap relative to higher-core instances.

Qualitatively, the F32-16amds_v7 balances high per-thread execution efficiency with generous memory and fast NVMe storage density on a single node. This resource mix suits memory-bound data processing, high-throughput compression pipelines, in-memory databases, and compute-focused analytical jobs requiring extensive workspace.

The system provides an expanded memory capacity of 256.0 GB (16.0 GB per core) and integrates a 3,780 GB local NVMe SSD for fast ephemeral scratch data, with no bundled GPU hardware. In benchmark testing, the high operating clock delivers top-tier single-threaded stress-ng compute, fast compression throughput, and strong lightweight LLM token generation, alongside median multi-threaded and memory bandwidth figures. The combination of strong single-core speed, local NVMe capacity, and a high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes this server profile well aligned with large-footprint in-memory databases, data analytics, compression pipelines, and memory-intensive transactional workloads.
